title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff and regional-failover thrashing
author: Asha Patel
commits: fix(slo-enforcer): add region-level minimum backoff window and jitter cap
fix(slo-enforcer): debounce concurrent failover triggers with token-based guard
test(slo-enforcer): add integration test for rapid failover/flapping scenario
ops: bump default backoff config in helm values for production
docs: update runbook with mitigation and rollback steps
description: Motivation: We observed a production incident where high request fanout + intermittent region congestion caused the SLO enforcer to repeatedly trigger regional failovers. That in turn caused capacity thrashing: failover would shift traffic, pushing another region over threshold which triggered another failover, and so on. The symptom was amplified by aggressive backoff decay and lack of a region-level cooldown. This hotfix reduces thrashing by (1) introducing a region-scoped minimum backoff window, (2) capping jitter to avoid pathological short retries, (3) adding a token-based debounce so only the first failover trigger for a region within the cooldown window proceeds, (4) smoothing the load-shedding score via a short EWMA (10s default) to avoid flip-flopping on momentary spikes, and (5) tightening the circuit-breaker cooldown policy so automatic re-enable is gradual and observable. Changes: updated backoff and circuit-breaker logic in services/slo-enforcer (backoff_policy.go, region_failover.go), added integration test that simulates rapid cross-region congestion, bumped helm default values (deploy/helm/slo-enforcer/values.yaml), added alert tuning (observability/alerts/slo_enforcer.yaml), and documented operational guidance and rollback steps (docs/ops/slo-enforcer-runbook.md). Testing and validation: local unit tests + new integration test passing; staged rollout to canary region for 2 hours with synthetic load replay; full rollout after canary SLOs stable for 30m. CI: initial run showed a flaky integration test which I fixed and re-ran; final CI green. Rollout plan: 1) deploy canary to us-west-2 (small percentage), 2) monitor SLOs, latency, and shed-rate dashboards + oncall channel, 3) if stable after 30m, increment to 20% then 100% over 45m, 4) if any SLO regression > 1% or sustained increased shed-rate, rollback to previous helm chart via release rollback. Backport: this change is safe to cherry-pick; follow-up PR will open backport for the 2026-02 maintenance branch. Notes: this is a targeted hotfix focusing on stability (no model/service API changes).

release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover to prevent thrashing
Introduce region minimum backoff window and capped jitter
Add token-based debounce to avoid concurrent failover storms
Smooth load-shedding score with EWMA to reduce flip-flop
Configurable helm values for backoff and cooldown
